local.title: The Garland County Detention Center
local.lead: A newer jail on open land — with a farm program already running.

facts.v: Opened in 2015 on 57 acres, a $42 million project run with direct supervision — staff work inside the housing units.
Designed to house 480, with room to grow to 600.
The 2026 budget carries $13,213,992 in the Detention Facility Fund, plus $246,768 for jail operation and maintenance and $282,000 in reserve — about $78 a bed a day.
The detention center is a University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture site, building skills and donating thousands of pounds of produce to Project Hope Food Bank.
Garland County Habitat for Humanity has built 170 homes in the Hot Springs area since 1995.
